title: IQM and Turkey's TÜBİTAK sign deal for 54-qubit quantum computer
html:
IQM Quantum Computers is set to deploy a 54-qubit superconducting quantum computer for the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBİTAK).

The IQM Radiance R3 system is scheduled to be integrated in 2027 and will operate under the national designation ARF Quantum.

Under an agreement signed by the two organizations, TÜBİTAK will fully own the quantum computer and retain local control over the hardware, execution data, and any IP the system generates. The Radiance R3’s quantum processor will directly integrate with the research council’s existing high-performance compute environment, with the system expected to support workloads across AI, cybersecurity, materials modeling, drug discovery, and logistics optimization.

It marks the second quantum deployment for TÜBİTAK, following a five-qubit QuanT processor installed at TOBB University of Economics and Technology in November 2024.

“I cannot be more proud of achieving another milestone for IQM Quantum Computers and extending our global footprint to Turkey with our sovereign & upgradable system R3 to be hosted at TÜBİTAK Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey,” said Sylwia Barthel de Weydenthal, chief commercial officer at IQM, in a post on LinkedIn.

“The strategic national objective was to provide Turkish researchers with a constant state-of-the-art flagship quantum system without relying on a foreign infrastructure. The system is fully owned by TÜBİTAK and will be integrated in 2027 and accelerate Turkey's ambition set up by the Minister of Industry and Technology.”

Founded in Helsinki, Finland, in 2018, IQM brings full-stack quantum computers and applications to HPCs, research institutes, universities, and business enterprises. The company operates quantum data centers in Finland and Munich, Germany, offering cloud-based access to its systems. It has delivered quantum systems to supercomputing centers in South Korea, Poland, Italy, and Taiwan.

In July 2026, the company began trading on the Nasdaq, having completed its Special Purpose Acquisition Company (SPAC) merger with Real Asset Acquisition Corp. (RAAQ).
summary: System is slated to be integrated in 2027
